<thought>From the spectrum the M+2 peak is about one‑third the intensity of the monoisotopic peak, which matches the characteristic 35Cl/37Cl isotopic pattern (≈3:1). The noticeable M+1 peak (~13 % of M) corresponds to the natural 13C abundance and indicates the presence of carbon. No other element shows a distinctive isotopic pattern (e.g., Br would give a ~1:1 M+2, S would give only ~4 % M+2). Therefore the elements that can be definitively identified are carbon and chlorine.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'Cl']</final_answer>
